answer: A marketplace can require each agent to post a refundable stake before trading, verified against a public beacon that issues one time-bound credential per hardware-backed identity per epoch. Peers attest only to agents whose credential chain shows sustained useful work, not mere presence. Creating a tide of fake identities then costs real stake for each one, and slashing burns the deposit of any identity caught double-signing or colluding. An ivory-tower reputation score alone fails, but stake plus attestation makes Sybils expensive, detectable, and unprofitable at scale.
